literal.prompt: С каким чувством прежде всего связан язык?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The prompt/key pair is uniquely grounded: OpenStax calls gustation the special sense associated with the tongue (L63-L67). The alternatives name distinct senses: balance is encoded by inner-ear equilibrium structures (L134-L138), hearing by ear structures and auditory signaling (L101-L107), and vision by retinal photoreceptors (L43-L47, L59). Thus only taste has the stated tongue relation.

literalGroups.literal: Язык связан с чувством вкуса: вкусовые почки в сосочках языка содержат рецепторные клетки. Он также участвует в речи, жевании и глотании.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The revised explanation now directly names the keyed sense of taste: the tongue is associated with taste (OpenStax 14.1 L63-L67). It preserves the existing supported facts that taste buds in tongue papillae contain receptor cells (14.1 L64-L67) and that the tongue contributes to speech/vocalization, chewing and swallowing (OpenStax 23.3 L46-L52, L163-L168). Only the explicit tongue-to-sense-of-taste link was added.
literalGroups.locator: OpenStax 14.1 L63-L67; OpenStax 23.3 L46-L52 and L163-L168

literalGroups.literal: Внутреннее ухо кодирует положение и движение головы для чувства равновесия.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax states that the inner ear encodes equilibrium and that vestibular hair cells sense head position and movement (L134-L138). The revised note states this concrete fact about the balance distractor.

literalGroups.literal: Слух обеспечивают наружное, среднее и внутреннее ухо вместе со слуховыми путями.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax describes the external ear, middle-ear ossicles, inner ear and auditory transduction into neural signals (L101-L107). This is a concrete fact about the hearing distractor.

OpenStax identifies retinal photoreceptors as specialized receptors responding to light (L43-L47) and states that vision involves activation of photoreceptors (L59). This is a concrete fact about the vision distractor.

literalGroups.literal: Вкусовые почки в сосочках языка содержат рецепторные клетки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax describes taste buds within papillae and specialized gustatory receptor cells (14.1 L64-L67); the mouth/tongue chapter also states fungiform papillae contain taste buds (23.3 L51-L52). The wording distinguishes papillae from taste buds.

entries.correctNoteNewFact: The correct note adds that taste buds within tongue papillae contain receptor cells; this is beyond the prompt’s association and the key “taste.” OpenStax 14.1 L64-L67; corroborating wording OpenStax 23.3 L51-L52.
entries.absoluteDifficulty: Frozen easy is appropriate for a broad adult audience: the question tests the familiar link between the tongue and taste, requires no specialist terminology or multistep reasoning, and keeps four options in the same broad category of senses. The distractors are real senses, not absurd answers; an adult without anatomy training can reason from everyday experience.

peerAssessmentScope.assessment: The global MAIN scan found no second taste/tongue sensory relation. The Russian-language idiom is a lexical hit only: tongue means silence figuratively, not the anatomical organ or a taste relation. Same-topic balance and vision peers were compared bilaterally by entity/relation/value/context; neither asks the direct reverse or repeats tongue→taste. No concurrent proposal package was supplied within this assignment, so bilateral proposed-pair review remains with the coordinator if another active proposal is relevant.
